title: Lalín–Rodrigue–Rogers unimodularity conjecture for Bernoulli–Euler polynomials
statement:
Let $B_m$ denote the Bernoulli numbers and $E_m$ the Euler numbers. For an even positive integer $k$, define

$$
P_k(x)=\sum_{m=0}^{k}2^m(2^m-2)B_mE_{k-m}{k\choose m}(x-x^m)(1+x)^{k-m}.
$$

Call a polynomial **unimodular** if all of its zeros lie on the unit circle. **Unimodularity conjecture.** The polynomial $P_k(x)$ is unimodular when $k\in2\mathbb{N}$. This conjecture arises from the observed fact that the corresponding polynomials in the secant zeta functional equation have zeros on the vertical line $\operatorname{Re}(z)=0$; the linear fractional transformation $z=(1-x)/(1+x)$ maps that line to the unit circle. It is presented as a numerical conjecture, and no resolution is supplied in the paper.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.3922

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2013).
source_name: Matilde Lalín, Francis Rodrigue and Mathew Rogers, “Secant Zeta Functions”, arXiv:1304.3922 (2013).
